sourceDocument.title: NASA-STD-8739.4A (w/ Change 4), NASA-STD-8739.3 (w/ Change 3) & Weller T0055745804 (Rev 08.2023) Operating Instructions
sourceDocument.publisher: National Aeronautics and Space Administration / Apex Tool Group LLC

procedure.title: Low-Voltage Wire Splicing & Soldering Training Procedure
prerequisites: Two disconnected, non-energized lengths of 20–24 AWG stranded copper wire
ESD-safe, fire-retardant silicone workstation mat with adequate cross-ventilation
Calibrated 40W–60W soldering iron station preheated to 350°C (660°F)
Protective eye protection donned before handling hot tools

requiredTools.name: Temperature-Controlled Soldering Iron & Stand
requiredTools.specification: 40W–60W station calibrated to 350°C (660°F) with rated safety rest (Weller WE 1 / WEP 70 / PH 70, Doc T0055745804 Rev 08.2023)

requiredTools.name: SAC305 Lead-Free Rosin-Core Solder Wire
requiredTools.specification: 0.8mm (0.031 in) diameter, 96.5% Sn / 3.0% Ag / 0.5% Cu, Rosin Flux Core (educational maker workshop selection; lead-free alloy reduces heavy-metal material-contact and ingestion concerns compared to leaded alloys; flux fumes require ventilation)

requiredTools.name: Precision Wire Strippers
requiredTools.specification: Calibrated stripping notches for 20–24 AWG stranded wire

requiredTools.name: Helping Hands / Third-Hand Fixture
requiredTools.specification: Weighted base with dual insulated alligator clamps

requiredTools.name: Brass Wire Tip Cleaner
requiredTools.specification: Coiled brass wire sponge with housing (or damp cellulose sponge)

requiredTools.name: Safety Glasses (PPE)
requiredTools.specification: Suitable protective safety glasses / eye protection

phases.title: Pre-Flight Electrical Safety & Tool Purpose Identification
phases.description: Verify non-energized conductors, don eye protection, and identify workshop tools.

phases.title: Conductor Stripping & Preparation
phases.description: Slide heat-shrink tubing, strip insulation without damaging strands, and pre-tin conductor tips per NASA-STD-8739.4 §19.7.1(a).

phases.title: Mechanical Splice Formation (Western Union Wrap)
phases.description: Form interlocking 3-turn Western Union wraps with no gaps, overlaps, or protruding ends per NASA-STD-8739.4 §19.7.1(b)–(d).

phases.title: Thermal Joint Soldering & Capillary Wetting
phases.description: Clean and tin iron tip to form thermal bridge, heat copper conductors, and apply solder directly to workpiece.

phases.title: Inspection, Heat-Shrink Insulation & Safe Shutdown
phases.description: Inspect smooth concave wetting fillet, contract heat-shrink tubing with hot air, tin iron tip, and power off station.

steps.title: Verify Non-Energized Circuit & Put On Safety Glasses
steps.instructionText: Confirm with 100% certainty that both wire conductors are completely disconnected from any power supply, battery, or energized circuit. Put on suitable protective eye protection before touching any heating tools.
steps.safetyNotice: High Electrical and Severe Thermal Hazard: Never perform soldering on energized (live) electrical circuits. Always verify power disconnection and wear suitable eye protection. This procedure is strictly an educational workshop exercise on disconnected, non-energized mock wires and is not certified for mains AC, automotive, or flight hardware.

sourceCitation.exactExcerpt: "Never work on voltage-carrying parts." "Protect your eyes by wearing eye protection." (Weller T0055745804 p. 14, Safety Information). Wearing protective eye protection and confirming circuits are unpowered are mandatory workshop safety rules.

trainingExplanation.whyItMatters: Soldering an energized wire creates catastrophic short-circuit, arc flash, electrocution, and molten metal expulsion risks. Educational training must strictly be performed on non-energized, disconnected low-voltage copper conductors.
trainingExplanation.componentInvolved: 20–24 AWG stranded copper wire and workstation circuit state
trainingExplanation.knowledgeCheckQuestion: Why must all electrical power be completely disconnected before starting any wire repair or soldering practice?

steps.title: Inspect and Identify Workshop Tools
steps.instructionText: Inspect each workshop tool on the bench: soldering station, safety rest, brass tip cleaner, SAC305 rosin-core solder wire, precision wire strippers, heat-shrink tubing, mini heat gun, and helping hands fixture. Verify the iron tip is clean and securely fastened.
steps.safetyNotice: Tool Familiarization: Inspect each workshop tool and confirm temperature calibration, safety stand stability, tip cleaner condition, and wire stripper sizing before applying heat.

sourceCitation.exactExcerpt: [Authoritative Technical Summary] Soldering system configuration comprising WE 1 supply unit, WEP 70 temperature-controlled soldering tool, and PH 70 safety rest with brass cleaning insert (Weller T0055745804 pp. 2–3, 14–16). Auxiliary workshop bench tools (wire strippers, mini heat gun, helping hands) are educational training equipment.

trainingExplanation.whyItMatters: Each workshop tool serves a critical mechanical or thermal role. Using incorrect stripping notches severs strands, dirty tips impede thermal bridging, and lack of helping hands leads to unstable, defective solder joints.
trainingExplanation.componentInvolved: Workshop toolset (soldering station, brass cleaner, strippers, third-hand fixture, solder wire)
trainingExplanation.knowledgeCheckQuestion: What is the primary function of the brass wire sponge compared to a wet cellulose sponge?

steps.title: Slide Heat-Shrink Tubing onto Wire A Prior to Splicing
steps.instructionText: Select a 25mm length of 3.0mm polyolefin heat-shrink tubing. Slide it onto one of the two wires (Wire A) and push it at least 75mm (3 inches) back from the stripped end so radiant soldering heat does not prematurely shrink the sleeve.
steps.safetyNotice: Positioning Precaution: Slide the heat-shrink tubing at least 75mm (3 inches) away from the stripped wire end to prevent radiant iron heat from prematurely shrinking the tubing.

sourceCitation.exactExcerpt: [Authoritative Technical Summary] Splice encapsulation requirement: "The tubing or insulation used for splices shall completely encapsulate the splice body..." (NASA-STD-8739.4A §19.2.6). Pre-positioning sleeving 75mm back on the wire prior to mechanical splice wrapping is an educational workshop sequencing practice for permanent splices, not a verbatim procedural mandate of the standard.

trainingExplanation.whyItMatters: Once two wires are spliced and soldered, a closed tubular insulation sleeve cannot be slipped over the junction. Installing it first and keeping it clear of the heat zone ensures proper post-solder insulation.
trainingExplanation.componentInvolved: Polyolefin 3mm heat-shrink tubing and wire insulation jacket
trainingExplanation.knowledgeCheckQuestion: Why must heat-shrink tubing be slid onto the wire before forming the mechanical splice?

steps.title: Strip Insulation from Both Wire Ends (20–24 AWG)
steps.instructionText: Using the calibrated notch matching your wire gauge (20, 22, or 24 AWG), strip 12mm to 15mm (approximately 0.5 inches) of insulation from the ends of both wires. Inspect the exposed strands to ensure zero strands are nicked or cut. Lightly twist the strands clockwise to restore the factory lay.

sourceCitation.exactExcerpt: "After removal of the conductor insulation, the conductor shall not be nicked, cut, or scraped to the point that base metal is exposed." (NASA-STD-8739.4A §10.1.1(d)). "The lay of wire strands shall be restored as nearly as possible to the original lay if disturbed." (§10.1.1(f)). Strip length of 12–15mm is an educational engineering specification suited to 3 Western Union wraps of 20–24 AWG wire.

trainingExplanation.whyItMatters: Nicking or cutting copper strands reduces conductor cross-sectional current capacity and introduces localized stress points prone to vibration fatigue breakage. Restoring the spiral lay prevents stray frayed strands.
trainingExplanation.componentInvolved: 20–24 AWG stranded copper conductor strands and wire stripper cutting die
trainingExplanation.knowledgeCheckQuestion: What physical defect must you inspect for immediately after stripping stranded wire?

steps.title: Pre-Tin Individual Stranded Conductors Prior to Splicing
steps.instructionText: Secure each stripped wire individually in the helping hands clamp. Wipe the heated iron tip on the brass sponge. Apply the flat face of the tinned iron tip against the bare strands and touch solder wire to the conductors until a thin, uniform coating of solder penetrates the outer strands. Ensure the tinned strands remain flexible and no heavy solder lumps form.
steps.safetyNotice: Thermal Burn Hazard: Hot soldering iron tip (350°C / 660°F) and molten solder present burn hazards. Support wire in helping hands clamp and avoid skin contact.

trainingExplanation.whyItMatters: NASA-STD-8739.4A §19.7.1(a) requires conductors to be pre-tinned prior to splice wrapping. As an educational explanation of this requirement: pre-tinning coats individual wire strands with alloy and flux, which helps prevent loose strands from separating ('bird-caging') during manual wrapping and facilitates rapid heat transfer during final joint soldering.
trainingExplanation.componentInvolved: Bare stranded copper conductor tips, solder flux core, and soldering iron tip
trainingExplanation.knowledgeCheckQuestion: Why does NASA-STD-8739.4A require conductors to be pre-tinned before wrapping a Western Union splice?

steps.title: Form Interlocking Western Union Mechanical Splice
steps.instructionText: Cross the two pre-tinned conductor ends at right angles approximately one-third of the way from the insulation. Tightly wrap each conductor end around the opposing straight conductor for a minimum of 3 complete helical turns. Ensure turns are tightly packed without gaps or overlaps. Trim any excess conductor wire flush against the core with flush cutters to eliminate sharp protruding ends.

sourceCitation.exactExcerpt: "There shall be at least 3 turns around each conductor and the wraps shall be tight with no gaps between adjacent turns..." (NASA-STD-8739.4A §19.7.1(b)). "The wraps shall not overlap and the ends of the wrap shall be trimmed flush prior to soldering to prevent protruding ends." (§19.7.1(c)).

trainingExplanation.whyItMatters: The Western Union wrap provides 100% of the mechanical tensile strength of the splice. Solder is an electrical conductor, not a structural glue. Tight wraps prevent tensile failure and flush ends prevent puncturing heat-shrink insulation.
trainingExplanation.componentInvolved: Pre-tinned copper conductor helical wraps and flush-trimmed wire ends
trainingExplanation.knowledgeCheckQuestion: How many complete turns are required on each side of a Western Union splice according to NASA-STD-8739.4?

steps.title: Clamp Splice in Helping Hands & Prepare Iron Tip Thermal Bridge
steps.instructionText: Clamp the completed mechanical Western Union splice horizontally in the insulated alligator clips of the helping hands fixture. Wipe the heated iron tip through the coiled brass wire cleaner. Immediately apply a small bead of fresh rosin-core solder to the tip face to establish an active liquid thermal bridge.
steps.safetyNotice: Thermal Burn Hazard: Soldering iron tip operates at 350°C (660°F). Always hold tool by insulated grip and keep helping hands firmly weighted.

sourceCitation.exactExcerpt: "Coat the soldering tip well with solder to ensure that there is efficient heat transfer between the soldering tip and the soldering area." (Weller T0055745804 p. 15, Handling the soldering tips). Helping hands clamping and thermal bridging are workshop application techniques.

trainingExplanation.whyItMatters: Clean metallic contact between tip and copper is impeded by surface oxidation. A small bead of molten solder creates a liquid thermal bridge that dramatically increases contact surface area, conducting heat into the wire core within seconds.
trainingExplanation.componentInvolved: Soldering iron tip, brass wire wool, and alligator clamp heat sinks
trainingExplanation.knowledgeCheckQuestion: What is a 'thermal bridge' in soldering and how does it prevent joint overheating?

steps.title: Heat Workpiece and Flow Solder into Mechanical Splice
steps.instructionText: Place the tinned iron tip against the underside of the wrapped splice joint. Wait approximately 1 to 2 seconds for the copper to absorb heat, then touch the solder wire to the top of the heated wraps opposite the iron tip (NOT directly against the iron tip). Allow solder to melt and flow through the helical wraps by capillary action for 2 to 3 seconds until all wraps are wetted. Remove solder wire first, then immediately lift the iron tip away.
steps.safetyNotice: Molten Solder & Chemical Flux Fume Hazard: Workpiece reaches 350°C. Rosin flux produces irritating vapors. Ensure cross-ventilation or bench fume extraction. Never inhale smoke directly.

sourceCitation.sectionHeading: Handling the Soldering Tips / Western Union Solder Flow
sourceCitation.exactExcerpt: "Apply solder directly to the soldering area, not to the soldering tip." (Weller T0055745804 p. 15). Solder flow requirement: "Solder shall wet all elements of the connection. The solder shall fillet between connection elements over the complete periphery of the connection..." (NASA-STD-8739.4A §19.7.1(f)–(g), p. 83). Molten alloy flows through helical wraps by capillary action (physical principle).

trainingExplanation.whyItMatters: Applying solder directly to the heated workpiece proves the copper has achieved wetting temperature. Capillary action pulls molten alloy into interstitial crevices between wire strands. Note on solder alloy: SAC305 (96.5% Sn, 3.0% Ag, 0.5% Cu) rosin-core is an educational maker training selection to reduce heavy-metal material contact and ingestion concerns during beginner practice, contrasting with NASA aerospace flight specifications that historically mandated tin-lead Sn60/Pb40 or Sn63/Pb37. Note that thermal flux fumes arise from both leaded and lead-free soldering, so active bench ventilation and eye protection remain mandatory regardless of alloy choice. This procedure is strictly an educational workshop exercise on disconnected, non-energized mock wires and is not certified for mains AC, automotive, or flight hardware.
trainingExplanation.componentInvolved: Western Union splice wraps, SAC305 rosin-core solder wire, and soldering iron tip
trainingExplanation.knowledgeCheckQuestion: Why must solder wire be applied directly to the heated copper joint rather than directly to the soldering iron tip?

steps.title: Allow Natural Cooling & Inspect Solder Fillet Workmanship
steps.instructionText: Allow the joint to cool completely undisturbed in the helping hands clamp for at least 20 seconds. Do not move the wires or blow air across the joint. Inspect the solidified solder: it must exhibit a smooth, shiny, concave wetting fillet across all wraps, with the individual outlines of the wrapped turns clearly discernible. Reject any joint showing dull crystalline texture, voids, sharp solder icicles, or excess blob buildup.
steps.safetyNotice: Burn and Disturbed Joint Caution: Allow joint to cool naturally for 20–30 seconds. Do not blow air on the joint or disturb the wires during solidification.

sourceCitation.exactExcerpt: "The appearance of the solder joint surface shall be smooth, nonporous, undisturbed..." (NASA-STD-8739.3 §13.6.1(a), p. 72). "Solder shall wet all elements of the connection... The solder shall fillet between connection elements over the complete periphery of the connection..." (§13.6.1(b)). "Connections shall be cooled at room temperature only." (§10.1.4, p. 62). Rejection criteria include fractured or disturbed connections, poor wetting, and excessive or insufficient solder (§13.6.2(b), p. 74).

trainingExplanation.whyItMatters: Disturbing or rapidly cooling a joint while the alloy transitions through its plastic phase creates microscopic crystallization cracks known as a 'cold' or 'disturbed' joint, leading to intermittent continuity and high resistance. Retaining visible wire contour proves optimal solder volume without thermal over-accumulation.
trainingExplanation.componentInvolved: Soldered Western Union splice and crystalline solder alloy matrix
trainingExplanation.knowledgeCheckQuestion: What visual characteristic distinguishes an acceptable solder joint from an oversoldered joint?

steps.title: Slide and Contract Heat-Shrink Tubing with Controlled Hot Air
steps.instructionText: Once the soldered splice has fully cooled to ambient room temperature, slide the polyolefin heat-shrink tubing forward and center it over the splice. Confirm the tubing extends onto the original wire insulation on each side by at least two wire diameters of the largest wire in the splice, using our workshop guideline of 6.35mm (0.25 inches) for clear visual verification. Turn on the mini heat gun (calibrated to 120°C–150°C) and sweep the hot air stream back and forth evenly along the tubing until it contracts snugly and smoothly around the splice with zero wrinkles or voids.
steps.safetyNotice: Thermal Burn Hazard: Hot air stream (120°C–150°C) and heated tubing present thermal burn hazards. Keep hands clear of hot air exhaust. Never use an open flame or direct soldering iron tip to shrink tubing.

sourceCitation.exactExcerpt: "The tubing or insulation used for splices shall completely encapsulate the splice body and extend over the wires’ insulation a minimum of two times (2X) the diameter of the largest wire in the splice." (NASA-STD-8739.4A §19.2.6). Extending the tubing by 6.35 mm (0.25 inch) onto the insulation is an educational workshop choice adopted for simple visual measurement, rather than a verbatim NASA dimensional figure.

trainingExplanation.whyItMatters: Insulation sleeving restores dielectric isolation and provides environmental protection and mechanical bend relief. Using an open flame or direct iron contact burns and perforates the polyolefin wall, compromising electrical safety.
trainingExplanation.componentInvolved: Polyolefin 2:1 heat-shrink tubing, mini heat gun, and original wire insulation jackets
trainingExplanation.knowledgeCheckQuestion: By what minimum distance must heat-shrink tubing overlap the original wire insulation on each side of the splice?

steps.title: Tin Tip, Return Iron to Safety Stand & Safe Power Down
steps.instructionText: Wipe the iron tip on the brass sponge and apply a fresh, generous bead of solder over the entire working face to seal the nickel-iron plating against atmospheric oxygen. Place the iron securely in its rated safety rest. Switch off the station power switch and disconnect the plug. Allow the tool to cool fully to ambient room temperature while securely seated in its safety rest before packing away.
steps.safetyNotice: Workspace Safety: Soldering iron remains hot after switching off. Always ensure tip is tinned and securely seated in its rated safety rest until fully cooled before leaving bench or storing.

sourceCitation.sectionHeading: Safety Information / Handling the Soldering Tips
sourceCitation.exactExcerpt: "Always place the soldering tool in the safety rest while not in use." (Weller T0055745804 p. 14). "Coat the tip with solder prior to storage if you do not intend to use the soldering iron for an extended period of time." (p. 15). "Leave the switched off soldering iron in the safety rest for at least 3 minutes until it has cooled down before packing away." (p. 16). In this workshop procedure, the tool is switched off, kept securely in its safety rest, and allowed to cool fully to ambient room temperature before packing away.

trainingExplanation.whyItMatters: Leaving a protective sacrificial solder coat on the tip prevents tip de-wetting and corrosive oxidation during cooling. Returning the iron to the safety stand prevents accidental bench fires or serious third-degree contact burns.
trainingExplanation.componentInvolved: Soldering iron tip plating, safety rest stand, and main AC power switch
trainingExplanation.knowledgeCheckQuestion: Why must a fresh coat of solder be applied to the iron tip immediately before turning off the power?

completionCheck.finalCondition: Two 20–24 AWG stranded copper wires joined with an inspected 3-turn Western Union wrap, pre-tinned and capillary-soldered with concave wetting fillet, fully insulated inside heat-shrink tubing overlapping original insulation by >6.35mm, with soldering station tinned, switched off, and cooled in its safety stand.
completionCheck.safetyVerificationText: Verify soldering station power is switched OFF, the iron tip is seated in the metal safety stand and cooled to ambient temperature, the soldered workpiece is cold to the touch, and all workshop consumables are safely stored.
